newsitem.title: USA: USWC crudes fall with WTI, conference saps trading.
newsitem.headline: USWC crudes fall with WTI, conference saps trading.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices ended weaker Monday with West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while discounts were stagnant as traders attended an industry conference, players said.
Activity was razor-thin, with no deals confirmed. Most West Coast traders gathered in San Antonio, Texas, where the National Petroleum Refiners Association (NPRA) convention runs through Tuesday.
Discounts for light grades were unchanged from Friday, with Alaska North Slope (ANS) last done at -$0.91 cents off WTI. Line 63 prices were idle at postings plus $0.95 to $1.00.
Outright ANS prices ranged $19.89/20.09, down 40 cents in notional talk.
Nominations are due Wednesday for April shipments on Canada's Trans Mountain Pipe Line Co, a pipeline official said. April barrels reach U.S. refiners 10 days into April.
Last month's shipments, which travelled from Vancouver to refiners in Washington state, averaged a unexpectedly high 105,000 barrels-per-day.
Outright prices for Kern River remained flat after two deals at 20 cents off postings last week. The grade was steady at $14.38/14.48 a barrel Monday.
